title: Demonstrate an understanding of plant propagation

lessons.title: Propagation and the right environment
lessons.html:
What is propagation?

Propagation means making new plants. Farms and nurseries propagate seedlings for vegetables, rootstocks and young trees for orchards, and cuttings for crops such as sweet potatoes, grapes and many ornamentals.

Two main types

  • Sexual propagation: from seed. Each new plant may be a little different from the parent. Used for maize, vegetables, many pasture grasses.
  • Asexual (vegetative) propagation: from a part of a plant, such as a cutting, tuber, runner or bud. The new plant is the same as the parent. Used for potatoes, sugarcane, grapes, citrus and fruit trees.

What plants need to propagate

NeedWhyHow we provide it
WaterSeeds need moisture to germinate; cuttings dry out fastRegular watering or misting; never waterlogged
TemperatureEach crop has a temperature range for germination and rootingTunnels, shade-net, heated beds in winter
Air (oxygen)Roots and seeds need airLoose, well-drained growing medium
LightSeedlings need light once they emergeShade-net in summer, full light later
Clean mediumSoil-borne fungi kill seedlings (damping off)Clean trays and sterile seedling mix
HumidityCuttings lose water through leavesMist systems, covers

Too much water and too little air in the medium is one of the most common causes of failure in a nursery. Too much heat in a closed tunnel in a Limpopo summer can kill seedlings in an hour, so watch tunnel temperatures and open vents as instructed.

A farm example

A citrus nursery keeps rootstock seedlings in a tunnel. On a hot day the worker opens the side vents and checks the trays twice a day, watering only when the top of the medium is dry. The seedlings grow strong without rotting or drying out.

lessons.title: Methods, tools and judging success
lessons.html:
Common propagation methods

  • Seed sowing: in seedling trays or directly in the field. Sow at the right depth, usually about two to three times the seed's size, and firm the soil gently.
  • Cuttings: a piece of stem is cut and planted to grow roots. A rooting hormone may be used.
  • Division: splitting a clump (for example some grasses and herbs) into smaller plants.
  • Layering: a branch is bent into the soil to root while still on the parent.
  • Grafting and budding: a bud or shoot of a good cultivar (the scion) is joined onto a strong rootstock. Used for citrus, avocados, apples and grapes.
  • Tubers, bulbs and runners: potatoes, onions, strawberries.
  • Tissue culture: in laboratories, for bananas and some other crops.

Tools and equipment

Seedling trays, growing medium, sharp clean knives or secateurs, grafting tape, rooting hormone, labels, watering cans with fine roses, mist systems and tunnels. Disinfect knives between plants to avoid spreading disease. Always label trays with crop, cultivar and date.

Successful or not?

SuccessfulUnsuccessful
Even germination across the trayGaps and patchy germination
Strong green seedlings with white healthy rootsSeedlings falling over at the soil line (damping off); brown roots
Cuttings with new roots and new leavesCuttings black, soft or dry
Graft union healed, bud growingBud black or dry, scion dead
Stocky plantsLong thin plants (too little light or too much heat)

Count and record the success rate (for example 92 of 100 seedlings came up). Report problems early so the cause can be fixed.

Safety

Use knives carefully, cutting away from your body. Wear gloves when handling rooting hormone and fungicides, and wash hands afterwards.

Key points

  • Seed gives sexual propagation; cuttings, grafting and tubers are vegetative.
  • Propagation needs water, the right temperature, air, light and a clean medium.
  • Avoid waterlogging and overheating in tunnels.
  • Use clean, sharp tools and label every tray.
  • Judge success by even germination, healthy roots and healed grafts.

quiz.question: Growing a new plant from a stem cutting is which type of propagation?
In grafting, what is the scion?

options.text: The root part of the plant
The bud or shoot of the good cultivar joined to the rootstock

quiz.question: Seedlings falling over at the soil line is usually a sign of…

options.text: Damping off, a soil-borne fungal problem

quiz.question: How deep should seed usually be sown?

options.text: On top of the soil only
About two to three times the size of the seed
Too little light or too much heat

quiz.question: Plants grown from cuttings are the same as the parent plant.
A propagation medium should be kept waterlogged so seeds never dry out.
Which are signs of successful propagation? (select all that apply)

options.text: A healed graft union with the bud growing
